text:
Unguyed, a flat web breaks its trees.

And the trees take all of it, eight metres up, as a lever. A 45 centimetre pine, green, breaks in bending at about 35 megapascals. Unguyed, the ten percent web works its trunk to a margin of 1.5, where a living tree should keep three; the five percent web, to 0.77, which is past breaking. So every anchor tree is guyed, and the guy goes where the owner put it: to the base of the next tree out, 8 metres behind. No ground anchors to buy or dig. The guy pulls 36 kilonewtons, 5/8 in rope, on a trunk at its strongest point, its roots.
